content:
elaine: Quick ask — for the launch copy and webinar we want to call out a clear performance claim. Need a final bench pack + reproducible methodology ASAP. Specifically: p50/p95/p99 generation latency, embedding latencies, quantized vs float variants, warmup policy, sample payloads, and the synthetic traffic profile you used. Can runtime produce a rerun that includes: 1) raw per-request CSV, 2) sample payloads we can ship to press, 3) exact docker/model hashes, 4) short readme on how to reproduce. Deadline: EOD Wed. @matt @devon :pray:

matt: Got it — we can run. Two clarifying q's: which model family to prioritize (rwft vs third-party), and target sequence lengths for gen/embeds? Also confirm traffic shape: steady QPS or bursty demo profile? We can produce a tarball with artifacts + a reproducible script.

devon: Prefer we surface rwft-7b and rwft-13b-quant for text-gen and embed-small for embeddings. Use seq len 128 for gen tests and 1024 for embedding latency. Traffic: emulate our demo — mostly steady with short 8–12s bursts (90/10 steady/burst).

sara: Marketing asks for p50/p95/p99 and token-level cost estimate for customer-facing claim. Also include a short 'what to call out' caveat if tail latency or OOMs observed. We need the sample payloads to be close to real product inputs.

matt: We'll run batch sizes [1,4,8] and produce percentile buckets + per-request CSV. Warmup command we'll run and include in README: ```python warmup.py --model rwft-13b-quant --requests 500 --seq 128``` KV-cache policy: persistent per-worker for 30m (so steady-state reflects cached prefixes). We'll attach curl examples and a minimal notebook that replays the per-request CSV. Scheduling reruns tonight; ETA ~18h. runtime-bot will push /artifacts/bench-2176549876.tar.gz when done.

leo: Note — quantized variants take a different kernel path; results are sensitive to batch size and sequence length. We'll log which kernel path picked and the compile flags.

runtime-bot: scheduled bench job 9872. Logs: https://ci.redwood/bench/9872 (streaming).

elaine: Thanks — please include an acceptance checklist for marketing: 1) tar.gz contains per-request CSV, 2) sample payloads (n=1000), 3) docker/image hashes, 4) a 1-page methodology README with warmup steps and how to read percentiles. Also include a 1-sentence blurb we can paste into slide notes describing the test setup.

matt: Will include a README + a tiny notebook that plots p50/p95/p99 and a heatmap of latency vs seq len. We'll also include a cost worksheet: tokens -> GPU-seconds -> $ estimate using our standard cost model.

devon: Small ask — add a cold-start metric (first request after worker spinup) and steady-state after ~10k tokens. Label metrics accordingly (cold vs warmed).

sara: FYI — can we shift the deadline to Thu morning? EOD Wed is tight for copy reviews. Also flag any quantized-quality caveats for comms.

matt: Shifting to Thu 09:00. If 13b-quant OOMs on our test hardware we'll fall back to 8-bit variant and note it in the README. We'll also include a short failures.log if we hit OOMs or retries.

elaine: Perfect — thanks all :heart: Please ping this thread when the artifact lands so we can start drafting the blog + slide narrative.

matt: Pinged when artifacts uploaded. Will post link here. :+1:
